sourcedFrom: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 (2022)
cleanIntro: The Equalizer field strips on a takedown lever turned down by hand, with no tool and nothing to press inside the frame. The one thing it asks of you is to keep your hand off the grip safety while the slide comes off and goes back on. Deep Clean is the magazine. The flush-fit and extended magazines come apart differently, and the manual covers both.

steps.title: Know which Equalizer you are holding
steps.action: Smith & Wesson asks you to work out which features your own pistol has before you handle it. Look it over and see whether it has a manual thumb safety lever. Equalizers are sold both with and without one, and where it is fitted there is a lever on each side of the frame. Every Equalizer has a grip safety at the back of the grip, and that is the part this strip is about.
steps.prose: The thumb safety decides what the first step asks of you, and the grip safety decides how the slide comes off. Smith & Wesson says the slide can be removed and refitted whichever way the thumb safety is set, so a pistol without one strips the same way. The only difference is that it skips the first instruction.
steps.quote: VARIOUS MODELS OF THE SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS ARE FITTED WITH DISTINCT FEATURES, WHICH MAY INCLUDE A MANUAL THUMB SAFETY.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Model & Features Identification, WARNING, p.13

steps.title: Thumb safety up, magazine out
steps.action: If your pistol has a manual thumb safety, push the lever up into the SAFE position. Then press the magazine release and take the magazine out of the pistol.
steps.prose: Taking the magazine out does not empty the chamber. Smith & Wesson warns that the pistol can still fire with the magazine removed if a round is chambered, which is why the next two steps work the slide and then look.
steps.quote: If your pistol is equipped with a manual thumb safety, place the manual thumb safety lever up in the “SAFE” position (FIGURE 40).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.27

steps.title: Rack it hard, then lock the slide open
steps.action: Keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction and your finger outside the trigger guard. Grip the serrated sides of the slide from the rear, hold the pistol upright, and pull the slide all the way back sharply to throw out any round in the chamber. Then hold the slide fully back and press up on the slide stop lever to lock it open.
steps.prose: Pull it fast and all the way. A slow or short pull can drag a round partway out of the chamber and leave it stuck in the ejection port. Holding the pistol upright lets the round fall clear.
steps.quote: Lock the slide open by holding it fully rearward and pressing up on the slide stop lever (FIGURE 43).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.28

steps.title: Chamber and magazine well both empty
steps.action: With the slide locked open, look into the chamber and then down through the magazine well, and confirm that neither holds any ammunition. Unload the magazine separately by pushing each round forward and out, with the bullet ends pointing away from you.
steps.prose: Check both places. A round that did not eject can lie in the magazine well, where looking only at the chamber will not show it. Smith & Wesson also warns not to rely on the loaded chamber indicator alone. Looking into the open chamber is the check that counts.
steps.quote: Make certain that the chamber (FIGURE 44) and magazine well (FIGURE 45) are clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.28

steps.title: No +P+ ammunition in this pistol
steps.action: Check the boxes of ammunition you shoot in this pistol. Smith & Wesson forbids +P+ ammunition in its firearms.
steps.prose: The book explains why: +P+ is not a defined pressure standard, so two boxes with that marking can produce very different pressures. This is the maker's ammunition rule printed in the Equalizer's own book, and the place to check it is while the pistol is empty in front of you.
steps.quote: “Plus-P-Plus” (+P+) ammunition must NOT be used in Smith & Wesson® firearms.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Ammunition, p.11

steps.title: Takedown lever down a quarter turn
steps.action: With the slide still locked open, turn the takedown lever down 90 degrees, clockwise.
steps.prose: No tool is needed and nothing has to be pressed inside the frame first. The lever stays in the frame: you turn it, you never take it out. Only turn it while the slide is locked open, because that is the position the book gives for it.
steps.quote: Rotate the takedown lever down 90 degrees clockwise (FIGURE 46).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.28

steps.title: Ease the slide closed
steps.action: Grip the serrated sides of the slide and pull it back until the slide stop lets go, then let the slide come forward gently to its closed position.
steps.prose: Let it forward under control, not with a snap. With the takedown lever turned down, nothing holds the slide on the frame once it moves forward, and a slide released hard is only being held back by your hand.
steps.quote: Close the slide by grasping the serrated sides and drawing it rearward (FIGURE 47), until the slide stop disengages, then carefully allow the slide to move forward to it’s “closed” position.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.28

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame, hand off the grip safety
steps.action: Hold the frame by its sides, not by the grip, and push the slide forward and off the frame. Keep control of the recoil spring as the slide comes free.
steps.prose: This is the step the Equalizer gets wrong in people's hands. Squeezing the grip, which is the natural way to hold a pistol, presses the grip safety. That raises the firing pin plunger lever into the slide's path, and the slide binds. Hold the frame by the sides and the slide comes off easily.
steps.quote: Keep tension off of the grip safety to allow the firing pin plunger lever to remain out of the way when removing the slide.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, NOTE, p.29

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out of the slide
steps.action: With the slide upside down, compress the recoil spring assembly slightly where its rear end rests against the barrel lug, then lift it up and out of the slide.
steps.prose: Compress it a little, then lift. Pulling straight back while the end is still seated against the lug only binds it. Keep a thumb on it, because the spring is compressed.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring assembly from the slide by compressing the spring slightly and lifting it up and out (FIGURE 51).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.29
steps.warn: Keep a hand over the recoil spring assembly as it comes out. It is compressed and can jump free.

steps.title: Barrel out, up and back
steps.action: Grip the barrel by its lug and lift it up and back out of the slide.
steps.prose: Lift it up and back, not straight up. The lug has to clear the slide before the barrel will come out, and lifting straight up only wedges it.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the slide by grasping the barrel by the lug and lifting up and back (FIGURE 52).
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, p.29

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You now have the slide assembly, the recoil spring assembly, the barrel, the frame assembly and the magazine. That is the pistol field stripped for cleaning, and it is as far as Smith & Wesson goes. Do not dry fire the pistol while the slide is off. Deep Clean covers taking the magazine apart.
steps.prose: The Equalizer has a hammer, and with the slide off there is nothing for it to strike. Pulling the trigger now is what the maker warns can damage it. Smith & Wesson also warns against taking the pistol apart any further than this. Anything past this point is a job for a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: DO NOT DRY FIRE YOUR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOL WHILE THE SLIDE IS REMOVED. DOING SO CAN RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE HAMMER OR OTHER INTERNAL PARTS OF THE PISTOL.
steps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Field Stripping / Disassembly, WARNING, p.30

deepSteps.title: Flush-fit magazine: press the catch through the floor plate
deepSteps.action: With the magazine empty, push a small, narrow tool through the hole in the floor plate to press down the floor plate catch underneath it.
deepSteps.prose: The catch is the only thing holding the floor plate on, and it sits on top of a compressed spring. Use a tool narrow enough to go into the hole without slipping, because a tool that slips off the catch can scratch the tube.
deepSteps.quote: Using a small diameter tool, depress floor plate catch through the hole in the floor plate (FIGURE 75).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Flush-Fit Magazine Disassembly, p.34
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure in the assembled magazine. Control the spring and other parts of the magazine so they do not fly out and cause injury.

deepSteps.title: Flush-fit magazine: floor plate forward and off
deepSteps.action: While holding the catch inside the tube against the spring, slide the floor plate forward and off the tube.
deepSteps.prose: Keep your thumb over the bottom of the tube as the plate comes off. Once the plate clears, the catch is the next part out, and the spring is pushing it.
deepSteps.quote: Slide floor plate forward off of the tube while holding floor plate catch in the tube (FIGURE 76) against spring pressure.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Flush-Fit Magazine Disassembly, p.34

deepSteps.title: Flush-fit magazine: catch, spring and follower out the bottom
deepSteps.action: Ease the floor plate catch, the spring and the follower out through the bottom of the tube. Note which way each one faces as it comes out.
deepSteps.prose: They go back in the same way they came out, so note the direction of each part now rather than guessing at reassembly. The book shows the parts laid out in order: tube, follower, spring, floor plate catch, floor plate.
deepSteps.quote: Remove floor plate catch and spring and follower out through bottom of tube.
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Flush-Fit Magazine Disassembly, p.34

deepSteps.title: Extended magazine: floor plate off by hand
deepSteps.action: The extended magazine needs no tool. Grip the floor plate firmly and slide it off while holding the floor plate catch in the tube against the spring. Then take out the catch, the spring and the follower through the bottom of the tube. This magazine also has a grip spacer/adapter, which comes off with them.
deepSteps.prose: The extended floor plate is held on by a friction fit rather than a catch showing through a hole, which is why it is pulled off instead of released. It has one more part than the flush-fit magazine, the grip spacer/adapter, and that part matters at reassembly.
deepSteps.quote: Hold the magazine as shown, grip the floor plate (FIGURE 83) and slide it off, while holding floor plate catch in the tube against spring pressure (FIGURE 84).
deepSteps.cite: SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR SMITH & WESSON® EQUALIZER™ PISTOLS — p/n 3015678                     REV: SMITH&WESSON_EQUALIZER_083122 — Extended Magazine Disassembly, p.36
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure in the assembled magazine. Control the spring and other parts of the magazine so they do not fly out and cause injury.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Brush excess firing residue out of the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish by running a dry cotton patch through the bore and chamber to remove the residue and solvent
If spent cases have been hard to extract, clean the chamber thoroughly with solvent

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME AND EXTERIOR
tasks: Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cleaning cloth
Remove all gun cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints from the outside surfaces, because moisture from fingers can start corrosion
Never move, adjust or change any internal part of the pistol that the manual does not tell you to

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe the tube, the feed lips and the floor plate
If the magazine has been taken apart, clean inside the tube and the follower before putting it back together
Keep this pistol's magazines with it: Smith & Wesson says a magazine will only work properly in the model it was designed for

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Put a single drop of high-quality firearms lubricant on each lubrication point shown in the manual
Do not over-lubricate: excess oil collects unburned powder and carbon residue, which can stop the pistol working properly
After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts inside and out with a high-quality gun oil
In a cold climate, use an oil weight that will not thicken in the cold
Avoid soaking the pistol in solvent or running it through an ultrasonic cleaner for long periods
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this pistol

reassembly: Put the barrel back into the slide: start the muzzle into the hole at the front of the slide, then tip the rear of the barrel down into place.

Fit the recoil spring assembly with its rear end against the barrel lug in the notch. The rounded parts of the rod go top and bottom and the flat sides face left and right. Make sure it is centred and clipped into the notch.
Check the hammer is cocked. If it shows above the frame, push it down and back until it is cocked.
Hold the frame by its sides and do not press the grip safety. Pressing it raises the firing pin plunger lever into the slide's path.
Hold the recoil spring in place and push the slide onto the frame rails, then on back over the rear frame rails.

Pull the slide fully back and lock it open on the slide stop lever, then turn the takedown lever 90 degrees counter-clockwise, back up to horizontal. If the lever binds and will not lock horizontal, turn it back down, reseat the slide and try again.
Pull the slide back until the slide stop lets go and let it go forward to its closed position.

Flush-fit magazine: put the spring, the follower and the floor plate catch back into the tube facing the same way they came out. Push the spring down until the tube's lips hold it, then put the catch on the spring. Press the catch down slightly and slide the floor plate on until the catch clicks into the hole. Push on the floor plate as if sliding it off to check that it is locked.

Extended magazine: put the follower and spring back into the tube facing the same way, and push the spring down until the lips hold it. Put the floor plate catch on the spring, then the grip spacer/adapter. Pull the spacer down at its sides to show the lips, then slide the floor plate fully to the rear until you feel or hear it snap on.
fncheck: With the pistol empty and pointed in a safe direction, check that the takedown lever is turned fully back up to horizontal. Pull the slide back by hand and release it several times: it should run forward fully to the closed position each time. Lock it open on the slide stop and release it again. If your pistol has a thumb safety, check that it moves fully up to SAFE and fully down to FIRE. Then put an empty magazine in, check that it latches, and check that the magazine release drops it.
